title: Streaming structured-response contract + tool-call fallback semantics
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Define clear, testable acceptance criteria for streamed structured responses and tool/function-calling behavior. This ticket covers: the streaming contract for partial JSON/NDJSON chunks, schema validation at both chunk and final boundaries, deterministic fallback modes when a tool invocation fails, backpressure and ordering guarantees, client-visible error semantics, and the observability/telemetry required for rollback decisions. The goal is to provide a single, unambiguous spec product + eng can implement and test against.
acceptance_criteria: Streaming envelope: Server MUST emit an initial metadata chunk that declares declared_schema_version and content_type before any schema-bearing tokens are emitted.

Chunk-level validation: Each streaming chunk that contains a complete top-level field (e.g., an object property) must validate against the declared schema subset; invalid chunk payloads must emit a structured error chunk describing validator_error and byte_offset.

Final-aggregation validation: On stream completion the server MUST perform a full-aggregation validation against the target schema. If aggregation fails, the final response must include an explicit final_error chunk with a human-readable summary and a machine-friendly error_code.

Partial-results visibility: Clients MUST be able to opt-in to receiving partial tool outputs (progressive_results=true). When enabled, partial outputs are actionable and accompanied by a confidence_hint field; clients can choose to call downstream tools on partial outputs.

Tool invocation envelope: Tool calls MUST follow a canonical envelope: {"tool_id": <string>, "call_id": <uuid>, "input": <object>}. The envelope fields must be present in both streaming and non-streaming modes.

Tool call idempotency: Each call_id must be idempotent for 60 seconds: repeated envelopes with same call_id and identical input are treated as retries and must not cause duplicate side effects in downstream connectors.

Failure modes + fallback policy: Define three fallback behaviors selectable by route: FAIL_FAST (propagate structured tool_error to client and stop further generation), FALLBACK_MODEL (route generation to a compatible fallback model variant), and IGNORE (log error and continue without tool output). Acceptance requires tests for all three policies.

Backpressure & ordering: When downstream tool latency increases, the runtime must apply backpressure to streaming clients after a configurable threshold (default 1s). Order of top-level fields must be preserved; reordering is disallowed.

Observable metrics: Each streamed call must emit events/metrics for stream_start, chunk_emitted, validator_error, tool_call_start, tool_call_end (with duration and success boolean) and stream_end. Metric names and tag schema are required in the implementation PR.

Compatibility: New streaming schema field declarations must be backwards-compatible with clients that only accept final JSON. Server must provide final consolidated JSON when content_type indicates final_json_supported=true.

Test harness: Provide an automated test suite that can simulate chunk corruption, tool timeouts, duplicate call_ids, and validate emitted metric events. Tests must be runnable in CI and included in runtime-1.20 branch.

Docs and samples: Console docs and SDK sample must include two end-to-end examples: (1) streaming tool invocation with FALLBACK_MODEL, (2) partial_results pipeline with IGNORE policy and client-side continuation logic. Acceptance requires doc sign-off from developer-experience.

Security & privacy: Tool input/outbound payloads containing pii must be redacted in logs by default; acceptance includes a log-inspection test that proves no raw PII appears in debug logs for a sample payload containing email/ssn patterns.
notes: Rationale: Customers want low-latency progressive tool outputs while retaining deterministic downstream behavior. We must balance usability (partial outputs) with safety (avoid duplicate side effects).
Trade-offs: Idempotency window (60s) chosen as compromise between implementation complexity and practical dedup needs for downstream connectors. Longer windows increase storage/coordination cost.

Edge case: Streaming binary blobs inside structured fields will be base64-encoded and validated against size limits; large blobs should be referenced via presigned_url pattern to avoid long-lived stream saturation.
Metrics note: Eng requested separate timer for validator_latency vs tool_call_latency to distinguish CPU-bound validation vs I/O-bound tool latency.

Compatibility note: For legacy clients that expect newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON), the runtime will also support an ndjson_mode toggle that emits independent complete JSON objects per line rather than a chunk-stream envelope.
